{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-wi-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"fd5142a6868c0ef5a458b393db87a77ea9fe4e2b7666bb3f9d6fb37ee7063a0f","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-wi-class-d:lineage:1","source_registry_sha256":"9dcfc0d0c3044debd01d4cb03103f48fb860797364a23b2cb56d36c868619a64","source_liveness_sha256":"4ca51030ff51b3372629ada1c05ad91f501dabccdcf7931dab678c717e7bb9b6"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Driving test requirements: vision, highway signs, knowledge and skills tests","heading":"C — Driving test requirements: the vision screening, the highway signs test, the knowledge test and the skills (road) test","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Driving test requirements: the vision screening, the highway signs test, the knowledge test and the skills (road) test
Knowledge domain: the four tests every new Wisconsin driver must pass before a license is issued — what each one measures, how it is scored, whether it needs an appointment, what it costs and what the examiner checks.

FACT_ID: sec01-F01 | anchor: A01
You need a valid driver license to drive on any Wisconsin public road, and getting one means passing a short series of tests: a vision screening, a highway signs test, a knowledge test and a skills test. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F02 | anchor: A01
The vision screening measures how well you see, and either the DMV or your own vision specialist can give it. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F03 | anchor: A01
Regular car and motorcycle applicants must have visual acuity of at least 20/40 in one eye, and glasses or contacts are allowed for that reading. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F04 | anchor: A01
Applicants must also have a 70-degree field of vision measured from the center of each eye. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F05 | anchor: A01
If you fail the vision screening, DMV staff explain the next step, which is a visit to a vision specialist with the Certificate of Vision Examination by Competent Authority, form MV3030V/T579. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F06 | anchor: A01
The highway signs test checks whether you can read and understand the signs that regulate traffic, warn drivers and give directions. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F07 | anchor: A01
The highway signs test has 15 questions, and you must answer 12 of them correctly, which is 80 percent, to pass. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F08 | anchor: A01
You can walk in for the highway signs test without making an appointment. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F09 | anchor: A01
The handbook covers every type of sign you may meet, and it tells applicants to study all of them before the signs test. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F10 | anchor: A01
The knowledge test measures what you know about Wisconsin traffic laws, and you can take it without an appointment. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F11 | anchor: A01
The knowledge test has 50 questions, and you need 40 correct answers, or 80 percent, to pass. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F12 | anchor: A01
Expect the knowledge test to take about 45 minutes, so arrive early enough to finish before the DMV customer service center closes for the day. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F13 | anchor: A01
Taking the tests at a DMV customer service center is free, and the DMV website also offers a free practice test. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F14 | anchor: A01
Applicants between ages 15 and 17 have the option of taking the knowledge test online instead, for a fee of $10. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-F15 | anchor: A02
The skills test is the same thing as the road test or driving test: a real-world demonstration that you can keep ordinary, reasonable control of your vehicle. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F16 | anchor: A02
A DMV examiner goes with you on the skills test and gives spoken directions, for example to turn left at the next intersection or to make a Y-turn. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F17 | anchor: A02
Unlike the written tests, the skills test needs an appointment, which you book through the road test page of the Wisconsin DMV website. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F18 | anchor: A02
Before the skills test starts, the examiner inspects your car to confirm it is safe to drive, looking at the horn, lights and signals, license plates, doors, mirrors and more. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F19 | anchor: A02
You should know how to work every vehicle control you might need during the test, such as the headlights, the wipers and the defroster. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F20 | anchor: A02
The skills test grades turning, intersections where you must stop, and the approach to intersections where no stop is required. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F21 | anchor: A02
It also grades driving through business or residential areas, changing lanes, and backing up. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F22 | anchor: A02
The test includes set maneuvers such as a Y-turn, a roadside stop and start, and parking, so practice each one beforehand. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-F23 | anchor: A02
The DMV website has more guidance on preparing for the skills test, and the handbook advises practicing every listed skill before test day. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0006]

Misconceptions: the highway signs test is a separate test from the knowledge test, not a few sign questions inside it; only the skills test needs an appointment, while the signs and knowledge tests are walk-in; the sharpness standard needs to be reached in only one eye, although the field-of-vision rule is measured from each eye; the car itself is inspected before the road test, so a broken light or horn can stop the test before it begins.
Mnemonics: both written tests share the same eighty percent bar, so think twelve of fifteen for signs and forty of fifty for laws; twenty-forty in one eye and seventy degrees from each eye for vision.
Glossary: skills test means the road test or driving test with a DMV examiner; visual acuity means sharpness of vision; field of vision means how wide an area you can see while looking straight ahead; Certificate of Vision Examination by Competent Authority means the form a vision specialist completes after a failed DMV screening.
Dynamic facts: the online test fee, the age range for online testing, customer service center hours and the DMV web addresses for practice tests and road test scheduling can change; confirm them on the Wisconsin DMV website.
